title: ScreamSeq local API version 1 request
description: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC subset on a private Unix socket: one request/reply per connection, string ids, no batch envelopes/notifications. Format-specific limits are enforced by the host.

oneOf.description: Atomic typed rack↔outer graph-stage auxiliary contribution. A stage is the combined row/persistent/ordinary bus stage, not one selected copy. Its auxiliary inputs feed every prepared copy; outputs sum audible wet/tail contributions. Input/output zero belongs to the main serial path and cannot address a stage. Omitted gain/enabled preserve the replaced connection.

Add a plugin-instrument note cable. New destinations wait for the next note-on. suppressAssignment atomically replaces an instrument’s implicit cable.
Edit one note cable by stable ID. Removed destinations release owned notes; retained destinations continue. MIDI channel 0 preserves the source channel.
Remove an explicit note cable by id, or suppress an implicit assignment by stable instrument identity. Specify exactly one. Releases cable-owned notes without stopping playback.

Read a rectangle containing at most 4096 cells; paginate larger patterns.
Atomic partial-field patches; unspecified fields survive. One undo step. dryRun returns before/after changes without mutation. Absolute volume uses volumeCommand=1, volume=0..64.

Bundles are validated in the isolated scanner, trusted, remembered for later launches, and the waiting rack and graph plugins resolve in place with their saved state. Call only after the user agreed.

Shared pattern tools, one document undo action; selection/channel/pattern/song scope. Song visits every allocated pattern once, including unused patterns. Up to 262144 selected cells. Dry runs return first 512 changed cells plus the full count. Volume/effect masks move command and value together. Numeric targets default to existing values. Exponential endpoints must be positive. Expand/shrink reject lost fields unless allowDataLoss is true. insertRows/deleteRows shift only masked fields within each fixed region; amount is 1..region rows. Insertion protects discarded tail fields, deletion protects removed leading fields, unless allowDataLoss is true. Pattern envelopes do not move.

List prepared rack processors and independent graph copies. Graph copies appear during playback preparation.
Read the prepared parameter catalog for one processor copy.
Read controlling sources and editing links; disabled sources remain visible.
Select the session parameter capture. Transient, no expectedRevision or song Undo. Idempotent unless clear is true.
Read bounded host-delivered values and source contributions after a cursor. Reset cursor when token changes; one shared selection per session.
Read paginated recorded automation in absolute 48000 Hz song frames.
Upsert, move or remove a recorded point by stable plugin identity. Prepared live edits preserve playback and other points, with unified Undo; dryRun is non-mutating.

heal.description: Explicit boundary edge indices for one connected processing subgraph, including branches and modulators, guarded by expectedRevision. Chosen edge gains multiply; unchosen branches remain when detaching. No implicit cross-product.

oneOf.description: Detach a serial effect chain and heal its main path atomically. Preserve auxiliary/modulation routes unless remove is true. Ambiguous branches fail unchanged. Optional positions share one Undo.

Read host physical ports, exact reusable graph copies and gained/delayed cable contributions from the adopted plan. Optional copy identifies graph/target/role/instrument/channel; route identifies the precise cable. Control records expose quantum endpoint values; Note Envelope sources additionally expose noteGate aggregate held/on/off/retrigger counters and lastFrame, not a raw MIDI event log. Use opaque audio keys for scope/listen. Measured false differs from silence; stopped values are historical.
Clear a prepared port clip/non-finite latch at the next observed block. Session-only; no song edit or Undo entry.
Choose one measured host port for bounded full-rate capture, or null to stop. Session-only, no Undo or song modification.
Read up to 4096 contiguous frames as at most 256 min/max buckets with audio-clock intervals. Optional Hann spectrum is computed off the audio callback. Includes capture/drop counts.
Temporarily listen to one observed host audio output. Linear 5 ms monitor crossfades preserve normal graph processing. Null restores the normal mix. Session-only, no Undo or song edit.
Read the requested monitor tap, monitor gain, pending crossfade and transition frames.

Package sibling processors/modulators or nested boundaries inside a reusable definition. Preserves DSP and real endpoint identities; default parent is the definition root. Returns a new group identity. One Undo; playback continues.
Rename or position a processing boundary without changing DSP. Identical values create no history.
Ungroup while retaining nodes, nested children and every cable. Explicit deleteContents deletes all descendants and their cables instead. One Undo.

Save a processing boundary as an independent reusable library recipe. Preserves enclosed processors/modulation; refuses external modulation dependencies. Original graph and assignments stay unchanged.
Song-level processing boundary. Preserves rack identities, routing and sound. Package sibling rack effects or child groups. Captured positions are saved in the same Undo transaction.
Song-level processing boundary. Preserves rack identities, routing and sound. Rename or move the boundary and all descendants.
Song-level processing boundary. Preserves rack identities, routing and sound. Ungroup while retaining processors and child boundaries.

Song-level processing boundary. Preserves rack identities, routing and sound. Copy a consecutive chain from one mixer owner into an independent library definition, including baseline settings and auxiliary ports. Original processors, routes and automation remain intact. Bypassed/missing members and cross-channel or nonconsecutive chains reject without mutation.

Atomically cut song cables by stable semantic endpoints. One Undo; dryRun leaves history unchanged. Cutting an implicit insert input or Master terminal never heals another route. Auxiliary branches remain intact.

formula.description: Bounded math expression. Required with scripted curve. start/end are normalized, t or beatOffset is segment progress, beat is pattern position in beats, beats is elapsed segment beats. Terminal segments extend to pattern end and end equals start.

audioStage.description: Typed channel graph-stage auxiliary tap; exclusive with audioBus/audioPlugin. Use a declared output >=1 and preFader=false.

parent.description: Existing song processing group. Source, optional edge and membership share one Undo; omitted creates at song root.

oneOf.description: Allocate a song-level control source, optionally connect to a stable rack parameter at zero depth and add to a processing group, in one Undo. No processor is replaced.

audioStage.description: Typed channel graph-stage auxiliary tap; exclusive with audioBus/audioPlugin. Use a declared output >=1 and preFader=false.

oneOf.description: Patch source settings; preserve identity/kind and other settings. Use graph.automation.set for pattern curves.
Atomically remove selected song sources and their modulation connections. Unknown/duplicate identities reject the whole edit.

Upsert one additive normalized contribution. Omitted fields retain previous values, or start at zero depth. Stepped targets require explicit quantized:true and usable discrete steps; read-only targets reject. All enabled contributions to one target share its quantization mode. Optional replace:{source,plugin,parameter} reroutes an existing edge in one Undo, retaining its range and flags. Missing old edge or collision with another destination rejects atomically.
Remove an exact set of modulation edges atomically. Unknown/duplicate edges reject; an empty batch is a no-op.

Presentation-only frames, comments and cable reroute geometry at song (graph:null) or reusable-definition scope. Replaces presentation; optional absolute node positions commit with it in one Undo. Never changes DSP or stops playback. Stable local annotation IDs and real cable endpoints survive projections.

Read existing envelope, pattern FX column and recorded automation provenance for a stable plugin parameter. Available stopped or unloaded; no DSP, revision or history mutation. Paginated bounded references retain original base-control semantics.
Read exact group audio ingress and egress identities, current/inferred dry routes, requested bypass and needsMapping without preparing plugins.

Bypass a real processing boundary while its contents keep running. A unique input/output dry path is inferred; ambiguous boundaries require an explicit dryRoutes map covering each outgoing boundary. graph:null selects a song group. One Undo; no per-member bypass substitution.
Replace sources mixed into a plugin input. 0 sums into Main in; 1–63 select named auxiliary/sidechain buses. Connected supported auxiliary ports enable automatically on playback; one document Undo.

params.description: Atomic direct plugin output to effect input upsert or exact endpoint replacement. Fan-in/out preserves serial ownership; input 0 sums into Main. Supported logical bus/channel slices only. Plugin instruments with supported physical audio inputs accept these routes and process after their audio dependencies. Disabled routes remain cycle-validated.

name.description: Nonempty UTF-8 name, at most 256 bytes.

target.description: Optional SK cell currently referencing id; clone and reassignment form one Undo step.

bypass.description: Host bypass for this processor in all copies; not a vendor parameter.

audioLayout.description: Host-captured logical-port to physical-channel fingerprint. A nonempty mismatch is rejected before processing; never clear it to silently retarget saved routing.

formula.description: Bounded math expression. Required with scripted curve. start/end are normalized, t or beatOffset is segment progress, beat is pattern position in beats, beats is elapsed segment beats. Terminal segments extend to pattern end and end equals start.

quantized.description: Explicit target-step mode. Required true for discrete targets; all enabled sources of one parameter share the same mode.

collapsedNodes.description: Stable real node keys displayed as compact cards; presentation only.

scratchCurve.description: Strictly increasing positions with endpoints 0 and 65536. Scripted points require a valid bounded formula.

name.description: Nonempty UTF-8 name, at most 256 bytes.
